ticks.note: Tick 1: `tenth` is initialised from the literal `0.1`, which KIELER rounds to single precision: 0.10000000149011612.
The input `f` is exactly the double 0.1, so `f == tenth` is false although both were written as 0.1. `whole = f * 10` stores 1.0 in an int: 1.
`f * 10` is 7.9; storing it in an int cuts off the fraction: 7.
−7.9 becomes −7: the conversion truncates towards zero, it does not round down.
0.5 is exact in single precision too, but `tenth` is still the rounded 0.1, so `equal` stays false. `whole` is 5.
